name: FormField
description: Label + control + hint/error in one unit with htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid wiring applied automatically.
designIntent: Every form control needs the same trio — label, hint or error, correct ARIA wiring — and hand-wiring it is where accessibility regressions start. FormField clones id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid onto a single-element child so the common case is one component and zero boilerplate.

props.name: id
props.description: The control's id — shared with the label's htmlFor and the hint/error ids.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label text (kept for screen readers even when labelHidden).

props.name: hint
props.description: Helper text under the control, wired via aria-describedby.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation error; replaces the hint, sets aria-invalid on the control, announced via role=alert.

props.name: required
props.description: Renders the required marker next to the label.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: Keeps the label screen-reader visible but hides it visually (sr-only).

props.name: trailing
props.description: Slot pinned to the far right of the label row (badge, link, action).

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Info icon rendered after the label; opens a tooltip with this text.
examples: Use your work email so teammates can find you.

props.name: labelPlacement
props.description: Stack the label above the control (default) or inline it to the left.

examples.title: Text input with hint
examples.code:
<FormField id="email" label="Email address" hint="We never share your email" required>
  <Input type="email" autoComplete="email" />
</FormField>
examples.description: The cloned child receives id, aria-describedby, and the label pairs via htmlFor.

examples.title: Error state
examples.code:
<FormField id="email" label="Email address" error={errors.email} required>
  <Input type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
</FormField>
examples.description: Error replaces the hint, flips aria-invalid on the control, and announces via role=alert.

examples.title: Search-style field
examples.code:
<FormField id="assignee" label="Assign to" hint="Start typing to filter">
  <Search options={people} onValueChange={setAssignee} />
</FormField>

antiPatterns.title: Don't rely on placeholder as the label
antiPatterns.explanation: Placeholders disappear on input and fail color-contrast rules. FormField renders a real <Label>; use placeholder only for example format.

antiPatterns.title: Don't nest multiple controls in one FormField
antiPatterns.explanation: The aria wiring (describedby/invalid) clones onto exactly one child element. For groups, use Fieldset or one FormField per control.
antiPatterns.example:
// Avoid: two inputs, one field
<FormField id="x" label="Names"><><Input /><Input /></></FormField>

antiPatterns.title: Don't duplicate ids across fields
antiPatterns.explanation: id keys the whole wiring — every FormField in a form must receive a unique id and the child must not override it with a different value.

accessibility.implementation: Renders <Label htmlFor={id}> and clones the same id onto single-element children
accessibility.userRequirements: Pass the control's real id as the FormField id

accessibility.implementation: aria-describedby points at the hint (or the error when present); errors render with role=alert
accessibility.userRequirements: Provide hint or error text — never both for the same state

accessibility.implementation: Sets aria-invalid on the cloned control when error is present
accessibility.userRequirements: Style the control with a destructive border/ring to match the announced state

accessibility.implementation: The asterisk is aria-hidden; native required semantics come from the control's own required attribute
accessibility.userRequirements: Also pass required to the control for native validation

guidelines: Name the thing, not the action
Say what failed and what to do
goodExamples: Password must be at least 8 characters

compositionRules.relationship: Wrap exactly one control — id/aria wiring is cloned onto it automatically
Use Fieldset (not FormField) when the label names a GROUP of controls
